story: Kutkh is a Raven spirit central to creation myths. In some tales he is created by a Creator and lets dawn onto earth by chipping away stones surrounding her. In others he creates himself, sometimes out of an old fur coat, taking pride in his independence. Kamchatka is created when he drops a feather while flying over the earth. Islands and continents are created by his defecation, rivers and lakes from his waters. He brings light in the form of sun and moon—sometimes tricking an evil spirit who captured the celestial bodies, sometimes being tricked himself into releasing them from his bill. His children copulate with other animal spirits, creating the peoples that populate the world. He interacts with Wolf, Fox, Bear, Wolverine, Mouse, Owl, Dog, Seal, Walrus and other spirits, often involving trickery, sometimes winning, sometimes being fooled. In one legend, the mighty raven Kutkh flew through the cosmos. Tired, he regurgitated the Earth from his gut, transformed into an old man, and landed on the empty land to rest. From his first footsteps emerged the first Mice. Curious and fearless, they entered his nose while he slept. His sneeze buckled the earth, creating mountains and valleys. His attempts to stamp them out formed the ocean. Further harassment led to a battle between snow and fire, creating the seasons. Thus the variable world emerged from interaction between Kutkh and the Mice. Kutkh gave mankind light, fire, language, fresh water, and skills like net-weaving and copulation, though he is also portrayed as foolish, hungry, thieving, and selfish.
